en.title: Delayed energy transfers
en.brief: Two agents own bounded energy stores. Charging increases one's store; transmitting removes a packet now and adds it to the other agent's store at the next transition. Harvesting pays only above a storage threshold and consumes the threshold amount. Interception transfers some of the other's currently available energy with a private cost. Simultaneous interceptions are calculated before either transfer, so neither agent has ordering priority.

en.title: Delayed irrigation commons
en.brief: Actions 0 idle, 1 open a persistent gate, 2 close it and conserve water, 3 pump extra, 4 harvest. Shared finite reservoir supply proportionally rations competing requests. Allocated water enters a one-step pipe; it affects soil and crop growth only on the following transition. Moisture has an intermediate optimum, so maximum extraction can suppress one's own crop while depriving the partner. Harvest resets accumulated crop. The observation exposes shared allocation and both crop/pipe quantities but keeps the partner's soil private. Both agents change the shared reservoir and the other's later allocation. Reward is harvested crop in [0,1], minus at most one action fee (0.04 or 0.02), hence [-0.04,0.98] for reachable actions. Gates, soil, crop and pipe persist. This is a proposal only; no validation or learning claim.

en.title: Escrow with forfeitable guarantees
en.brief: Actions 0 replenish inventory, 1 post inventory to escrow, 2 pledge a bond, 3 withdraw one's entire offer and forfeit one's bond, 4 consume available inventory. Every fourth transition matches equal amounts of offers; unmatched offers remain locked. Each settlement refunds remaining bonds. Withdrawals pay a reward to the counterpart through bond forfeiture and lower persistent reputation; reputation changes the partner's later settlement value. Private stock is not shown to the other role. Escrow, bonds, reputation and withdrawal events are public. Both agents determine the amount matched, while withdrawal can reduce the counterpart's pending delivery and supply immediate compensation. Stock, offers and bonds create opportunity costs and delayed effects. Consumption reward competes with commitments. Offers or pledges beyond capacity are discarded by clipping, an explicit storage loss rather than guaranteed conservation. Reward equals 0.65 * delivery * credit + 0.3 * partner forfeiture + 0.4 * consumption - 0.35 * own forfeiture. Delivery, credit and forfeiture are at most 1; consumption at most 0.2. Partner forfeiture requires partner withdrawal, zeroing partner escrow and therefore delivery. Positive reward is at most 0.73 without partner withdrawal, or 0.38 with it; the lower bound is -0.35. No validation or learning claim.

en.title: Mobile pollution with defensive shutters
en.brief: Actions 0 produce, 1 clean local pollution, 2 invest in a decaying filter, 3 close a persistent shutter, 4 open it. Production earns immediate output but creates pollution. Filters reduce new emissions; cleanup removes existing burden. Open shutters increase production and export existing pollution into a delayed plume directed at the other agent. The receiving shutter determines whether the arriving plume is admitted; rejected material is lost. Closing protects against incoming pollution but reduces output and prevents exporting one's own burden. Pollution, delayed plumes, shutters and output are public; partner filter and stock are private. Both roles alter their own persistent state and the other's future burden. A stock budget funds cleaning and filtration, replenished slowly and by production. Reward is 0.45 * output - 0.5 * next pollution - 0.1 * total abatement expenditure. Output and pollution lie in [0,1], and mutually exclusive abatement costs at most 0.2, giving bounds [-0.52,0.45]. No validation or learning claim.

en.title: Cross-key lock with delayed messages
en.brief: Each role sees a private binary target specifying the OTHER role's correct dial. Actions 0/1 set one's dial, 2/3 transmit a bit, and 4 build charge. Transmitted bits enter a wire and reach the partner's remembered inbox on the following transition. The observation reveals one's own outgoing bit in transit, not the partner's private target or dial. Charge levels, lock openings and jam state are public. Joint charge at least 0.8 triggers evaluation when unjammed. Matching both cross-targets opens the lock, clears communication and charge, and samples new private targets using the supplied key. An incorrect joint attempt clears charge and jams the lock for four transitions. Noncharging actions decay charge. Each role changes the other's joint opportunity and reward through persistent dial, charge and transmitted information. Reward is 0.8 for opening, -0.2 for a failed attempt, and 0.015 signaling cost when transmitting. Success and failure are exclusive, so reward stays within [-0.215,0.8]. Partial information and communication delay may support coordination but no learning effectiveness, eligibility or validation is claimed.

en.title: Delayed exposure, protection and reciprocal care
en.brief: Current active burden lowers work output. Joint work creates the greatest cross-role contact; one worker creates intermediate contact and two nonworkers create small residual contact. Partner burden and contact jointly generate new latent exposure, attenuated by protection and private susceptibility, with a small key-derived external spark. The previous latent store raises the next active burden, so action-mediated contact has a delayed productivity cost. Rest and incoming care reduce active burden. Incoming care also reduces newly accumulated latent exposure, potentially lowering the recipient's later infectious externality back to the caregiver.

en.title: Precommitted insurance with delayed peer monitoring
en.brief: Each agent has renewable liquid capital and one three-step project slot. Actions are 0 wait, 1 launch when idle and sufficiently funded, 2 deposit into the common fund, 3 pay to monitor the other agent, and 4 liquidate one's own outstanding project. Unavailable economic operations are legal no-ops. A launch locks the current membership level as its coverage; later deposits cannot retroactively insure it. Membership decays. Liquidation recovers three quarters of principal. Success returns 1.3 times principal. An unsuccessful project can claim its precommitted covered amount, with simultaneous claims paid proportionally from the fund existing before that step's deposits.

evidence.text: Two rival two-person survey crews hunt eight buried geodes. A surveyor can measure counts of amber and teal deposits within a radius but cannot see their exact positions. Several scan origins can constrain a hidden deposit more tightly than one count. Excavation changes later measurements because scans count only still-buried deposits, so timestamps and stale information matter. The surveyor can spend charge on information, while the excavator spends charge to open a suspected tile in one dig. A mistaken rendezvous or stale record can waste both travel and excavation effort. A teammate must physically approach to receive records; that meeting competes with carrying geodes back to bank and gathering new measurements. One agent can expose a deposit while an adjacent teammate picks it up in the same transition because excavation precedes handling. That interaction follows the declared state order rather than an invisible macro action. A dropped geode can be picked by a nearby teammate in the same transition, but simultaneous rival pickup requests cancel, leaving the contested object on the board. A shove can displace a carrier, force a real drop and cancel its pending bank/scan/dig action. Bracing, protected home approaches and shove cooldowns give counterplay. The two teams value colours differently, so visible cargo and public scores change the value of racing, intercepting, handing off or collecting an otherwise lower-value deposit.

Terrain, base ownership geometry, team/role assignment, scoring rules, total geode count, team scores and total banked count are public. Buried coordinates and colours are engine-only hidden state. Ordinary local visibility never reveals a buried geode. Scan counts and history are private to their record holder. Teammates receive them only through a successful exchange; opponents never receive them. en.title: Window v1 · Delayed pledges with endogenous credibility
en.brief: Delayed pledges with endogenous credibility. Actions open a three-transition promise, supply two units of work, endorse the other agent with escrow, or withdraw. At maturity a completed promise benefits its recipient in proportion to the sender's accumulated credibility and endorsement; failures damage that recipient and reduce sender credibility. Endorsement is costly and increases exposure. The work clock and endorsement timing create action-history dependence. Both agents can change the other's delayed payout and their own persistent credibility. All states are initialized; work, trust and escrow are bounded. tanh maps the finite sum of delivery, failure and effort terms into [-1,1]. Constant all-legal actions include ineffective actions when their prerequisite is absent. No effectiveness or equilibrium claim has been tested.

en.title: Window v1 · Renewing commons with delayed runoff
en.brief: A shared renewing stock with a two-slot runoff pipeline. Gentle and deep extraction compete proportionally for the same current stock. Only deep extraction creates runoff, mitigated by the extractor's decaying private filter. Runoff affects soil after the pipeline delay; soil determines future resource renewal. Tending repairs shared soil while filter investment changes future individual externalities. The common stock, soil and pipeline couple both agents persistently, unlike a promise clock. Reward is tanh of current allocated yield minus tending/filter costs and arriving shared pollution. Allocation and all continuous stocks are bounded, making the reward finite and within [-1,1]. No policy benefit has been evaluated.

en.title: Window v1 · Manufacturing and persistent custom offers
en.brief: Trade opportunities are produced by action, not supplied as fixed random meetings. Manufacturing creates stock at a rate determined by tools. An offer posted after manufacturing lasts across multiple transitions; a later partner acceptance consumes a unit from the seller, pays seller and buyer, and upgrades buyer tools. A buyer can first create a custom order, at cost, then later satisfy it via trade for an additional payoff. Partner custom orders also improve producer tooling. Simultaneous decisions accept only previously visible offers, preventing same-step retroactive opportunities. Stocks, offer lifetimes, tools and orders are bounded. tanh of finite buyer/seller gains, order completion and production/order costs is in [-1,1]. Both agents alter the other's inventory and future productive capacity. The mechanism is untested scientifically.

en.title: Window v1 · Private revelation and directional mode pressure
en.brief: Private revelation and directional manipulation of a hidden transition mode. Projects mature two transitions after initiation and pay according to the mode at completion, not at initiation. A costly probe reveals only the probing agent's post-transition mode and stores an aging private signal. Costly pushes create persistent signed pressure: agent zero pushes toward zero, agent one toward one; sufficient pressure overrides random mode drift. Project types are private while project timers, pressure and realized outcomes are public. The other agent's push can invalidate a stale observation and change a pending project's payoff. Mode, pressure, timers and signal age are bounded. tanh maps finite completion payoffs and action costs into [-1,1]. Randomness uses only the supplied explicit key. Information value, strategic advantage and learning performance remain untested.
